A table of future value interest factors for an annuity of $\text{\textdollar}1$ is shown.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & \textit{Interest rate per period as a decimal} \\ \hline N \backslash r & 0.002 & 0.006 & 0.020 & 0.024 & 0.060 & 0.240 \\ \hline 10 & 10.09048 & 10.27437 & 10.94972 & 11.15211 & 13.18079 & 31.64344 \\ \hline 20 & 20.38460 & 21.18211 & 24.29737 & 25.28909 & 36.78559 & 303.60062 \\ \hline 30 & 30.88646 & 32.76227 & 40.56808 & 43.20983 & 79.05819 & 2640.91639 \\ \hline 40 & 41.60026 & 45.05630 & 60.40198 & 65.92708 & 154.76197 & 22\,728.80260 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

questions.stem_latex:
In a reducing-balance loan, an amount $\text{\textdollar}P$ is borrowed for a period of $n$ months at an interest rate of $0.25\%$ per month, compounded monthly. At the end of each month, a repayment of $\text{\textdollar}M$ is made. After the $n$th repayment has been made, the amount owing, $\text{\textdollar}A_n$, is given by

$$A_n=P(1.0025)^n-M\left(1+(1.0025)^1+(1.0025)^2+\cdots+(1.0025)^{n-1}\right).$$

(Do NOT prove this.)

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
Jane borrows $\text{\textdollar}200\,000$ in a reducing-balance loan as described.

The loan is to be repaid in 180 monthly repayments.

Show that $M=1381.16$, when rounded to the nearest cent.

parts.label: b
parts.latex:
After 100 repayments of $\text{\textdollar}1381.16$ have been made, the interest rate changes to $0.35\%$ per month.

At this stage, the amount owing to the nearest dollar is $\text{\textdollar}100\,032$. (Do NOT prove this.)

Jane continues to make the same monthly repayments.

For how many more months will Jane need to make full monthly payments of $\text{\textdollar}1381.16$?

parts.label: c
parts.latex:
The final repayment will be less than $\text{\textdollar}1381.16$.

How much will Jane need to pay in the final payment in order to pay off the loan?
